envelope.decodeDocs:
Normalize WorkOS's two error envelopes into one shape. `code` and the
OAuth-style `error` collapse to a single discriminator; `message` prefers the
human field of whichever envelope is present.

errors.docs:
WorkOS surfaces two error envelopes: `{ code, message }` and the OAuth-style
`{ error, error_description }`. Both are normalized to a single discriminator
by the matcher; the classes below are the ones the generator lifted from the
spec's discriminated `oneOf` error tables.
errors.codeDocs:
The spec's discriminated `oneOf` error tables enumerate 95 distinct codes
across the API; one class per documented code, in this exact per-class shape,
ordered alphabetically by discriminator code — the same order as CODE_ERRORS
and every declared-errors tuple.

organizations.docs:
Uniform per-operation blocks: input schema + type, a declarative descriptor,
and a thin exported function that dispatches through `run`.

userManagement.docs:
The authenticate operation is the error-rich showcase: WorkOS returns
distinct 400/403 discriminator codes that map to distinct tagged errors, and
both the request secrets (`client_secret`, `password`) and the response
tokens (`access_token`, `refresh_token`) are redacted.

organizations.create.docs: Create an organization in the current environment.

organizations.get.docs: Fetch a single organization by id.

organizations.delete.docs: Permanently delete an organization. Cannot be undone.
organizations.delete.errorsDocs:
The spec documents only 200/202/403 for delete — a missing organization
returns 403, not 404 — so `Forbidden` is the only declared error. (v1 also
listed `NotFound`, which delete cannot actually produce.)

organizations.list.docs: Fetch a single page of organizations.

userManagement.authenticateWithPassword.docs:
Authenticate a user with an email and password (the `password` grant).

`client_secret` and `password` are `Redacted<string>` — wrap plaintext with
`Redacted.make(...)`. On success, `access_token`/`refresh_token` are likewise
`Redacted<string>`. Failures discriminate: `InvalidCredentials`,
`MfaEnrollment`, `EmailVerificationRequired`, `OrganizationSelectionRequired`,
`InvalidGrant`, and so on — never a single opaque `BadRequest`.
